messages:
lena_cs: Onboarding hiccup with VitalTrack. Python SDK in their staging runs into 401 then a flood of 429s during their load-run at 14:05 UTC. Can eng help triage?

marco_eng: Can you paste a small log sample? 401->429 usually indicates token validity timing + refresh fanout or missing client-side caching.

lena_cs: Log: 
```
[2026-03-23T14:05:03Z] token.fetch -> 200 {tok: aaa}
[2026-03-23T14:05:03Z] client.call -> 401 {"err":"token not active"}
[2026-03-23T14:05:04Z] token.fetch -> 200 {tok: bbb}
[2026-03-23T14:05:04Z] client.call -> 429 {"err":"rate_limit.exceeded"}
```
They spin up many short-lived test containers, each does fetch+call.

ivan_ops: Their containers use ephemeral keys per-run and no shared cache. Also their CI images have drift of ~4s vs our servers.

marco_eng: Two fixes: client-side: use a shared cache (Redis or in-process) so only one token refresh per service instance. Add jitter and a short TTL < token expiry. Server-side: small tolerance for nbf <= 5s and merge identical rapid refreshes into a single rate-limiter bucket.

lena_cs: Recommended Python snippet for customer (simple Redis-backed guard): 
```
# pseudo
val = redis.get('rtoken')
if not val:
  if redis.setnx('rtoken:lock', 1):
    token = fetch_new()
    redis.set('rtoken', token, ex=60)
    redis.delete('rtoken:lock')
  else:
    time.sleep(0.05 + random()*0.2)
    token = redis.get('rtoken')
```
This prevents N concurrent fetches.

marco_eng: Also advise them to add a 1-2s retry on 401 before triggering parallel refreshes, and to ensure NTP is enabled in the image.

ivan_ops: We can also temporarily raise their burst allowance for onboarding for 12h. Billing ok with that if CS requests it.

ci-bot: AUTO: Ticket VTL-11234 opened, assigned to lena_cs.

lena_cs: I've asked them to enable chrony in the image and to deploy the redis-lock snippet to CI. They'll test in 2 hours. I'll request 12h burst from billing.

marco_eng: We'll add a short note in DevEx about Redis token caching pattern + retry-on-401 heuristic.

lena_cs: Update: after adding a shared cache and small jitter, their 500-concurrent test showed no 401/429 cascade. Closing. Thanks team! :slightly_smiling_face:
